flawed_step: The universal claim fails: 3-regularity plus 3-connectivity does not force a Hamiltonian cycle (the Petersen graph is a counterexample).
counterexample: Petersen graph on vertices 0..9: outer cycle 0-1-2-3-4-0, spokes i-(i+5), inner pentagram 5-7,7-9,9-6,6-8,8-5. It is simple, 3-regular, and 3-connected (standard: connectivity 3). Not Hamiltonian: a Hamiltonian cycle uses an even number of spokes, so 2 or 4. With 2 spokes, the outer part is a 4-edge path whose ends i,i+1 are adjacent on the outer cycle, and the inner part is a 4-edge path whose ends 5+i,5+i+1 must be adjacent on the pentagram, but pentagram neighbours differ by ±2: contradiction. With 4 spokes (spoke 0-5 unused, by symmetry), the forced edges are 4-0,0-1,2-3,5-7,5-8,6-9 plus spokes 1-6,2-7,3-8,4-9. These contain the 5-cycle 0-1-6-9-4-0, so they do not form a single 10-cycle: contradiction.
assessment_summary: False. The Petersen graph is a 3-regular, 3-connected graph with no Hamiltonian cycle. This was checked by a case split on the number of spokes used (2 or 4); both cases lead to a contradiction.
